sequence.description: The log's head once the command committed: its last event, or the head it saw when it appended none.

changed.description: False for a command that was accepted and changed nothing, so appended no event.

sequence.description: The log's head when the command was rejected.

reason.description: Why the command was rejected, the code of its error: not_found when its target does not exist.

code.description: A stable error code in snake case.

error.description: The rejection as an error: its code (the reason), a message for people and structured data.

receipt.description: A command's receipt: accepted (with the head sequence after it and whether it changed anything) or rejected (with the reason and the error). A retry with the same commandId answers the same receipt.

result.description: The method's result, present when this request applied the command; absent on a retry and on a rejection.

sessionId.description: A session's id: a version 4 UUID the creating client mints (never the provider's resume id), kept in lowercase.

ceiling.description: The ceiling it was clamped to.

clamped.description: Whether the mode got is below the one asked for; false when none was asked for, since a default applied then and nothing was clamped.

anyOf.description: Why a mode was lowered: ceiling (above the ceiling, lowered to it), or unavailable (the mode it would have had is one the account lists as unavailable, so the next lower available one).

clampReason.description: Why the mode asked for was lowered; null when it was not, or when none was asked for.

mode.description: The mode asked for, the one the session got under the caller's ceiling and its account's modes, and the clamp.

runId.description: A run's id: a version 4 UUID the environment mints when the run starts or is adopted.

mode.description: The mode the live run was changed to: the session's, clamped to the run's own ceiling too.

live.description: The live run the mode was applied to at once; null when none was live or its adapter cannot change a running run's mode, so it applies at the next run.
